summary: example-js-project preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<platform>.zip, unpacks it to a temporary directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against the sibling file math_init.js (or uses a pre-existing system bun binary if present). math_init.js is a 727 KB single-line Bun-compiled CJS bundle ('// @bun @bun-cjs') with a rotating string/constant array (WV8StW rotates n7gIxM) and hex-named identifiers — its behavior is not reviewable statically. The package advertises Vue example content and ships empty author/description metadata; a Bun-compiled opaque binary is unrelated to that stated purpose. The preinstall hook auto-executes on `npm install`, so any code embedded in math_init.js runs on the installer's host with the installer's privileges. This is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern: Node fetches a second language runtime specifically to execute a sibling payload that Node itself would not run, using purpose-mismatch and obfuscation to hide the payload's behavior.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
